title: SIMP topology optimization (optimality criteria) over the validated hex8 reference FEA

governing_equations.name: minimum compliance problem
governing_equations.expr: min_rho  c(rho) = F^T u(rho)   s.t.  K(rho) u = F,  mean(rho|design) = volfrac,  0 <= rho <= 1
governing_equations.description: Classic density-based topology optimization: minimize compliance at a fixed material budget over the design-region voxels; frozen voxels are re-pinned to 1 and void to 0 every iteration.

governing_equations.name: SIMP interpolation
governing_equations.expr: E_e = floor + rho_e^p (E0 - floor),  p = 3 by default
governing_equations.description: Penalized element modulus drives intermediate densities toward 0/1; the FEA underneath is the pinned engine.verify.reference_fea (see ace_fea manifest).

governing_equations.name: optimality-criteria update + cone filter
governing_equations.expr: rho_new = clip(rho (dc/drho / lambda)^0.5, move);  rho_phys = H rho / H 1
governing_equations.description: top88-style OC update with bisection on the volume multiplier lambda, and a cone density filter of radius filter_radius_vox (masked to the design region) against checkerboarding.

assumptions: Everything the underlying ace_fea manifest assumes (linear elastic, small strain, hex8 voxel grid).
Single load case, compliance objective only — no stress, frequency, or multi-load objectives.
Design region = voxels solid in the INITIAL geometry AND kind 'design'; loads/fixtures must sit on frozen regions or they can be optimized away (documented runner contract).
The thresholded (iso 0.5) as-built part is re-analyzed with BINARY occupancy — reported as_built numbers are for the printable geometry, not the gray-density design.
Local optimizer: OC converges to a local optimum of a non-convex problem; no global-optimality claim.

boundary_conditions.fixtures: identical selector engine and semantics as ace_fea (clamped/pinned/slider on grid nodes).
boundary_conditions.loads: identical to ace_fea; loads apply only on ACTIVE elements — hence the frozen-region requirement around load application.
boundary_conditions.selector_count_unit: nodes (active grid nodes touching the selected active elements)

inputs.geometry: mm (ops+solid via kernel sampling, or a density .npy)

outputs.compliance_first/compliance_last: J (F^T u of the gray SIMP design)
outputs.volume_fraction_achieved: dimensionless mean physical density over the design region

discretization.method: density-based topology optimization (SIMP) on the hex8 voxel grid
discretization.element: one design variable per voxel; OC update, move limit 0.2 default, density floor 0.02
discretization.notes: Stops at max_iters, change < tolerance, or 0.8x time_budget_s; stop_reason is in the receipt.

validation.ground_truth: No closed-form optimal topology exists; the pins are exact falsifiable properties on a cantilever whose FEA is itself pinned: (A) OC descent — compliance_last <= 0.9 x compliance_first; (B) material-removal monotonicity — the thresholded as-built part (subset of the solid domain, same grid/load) deflects >= the full solid; (C) volume honesty — achieved fraction within 0.02 of volfrac; (D) the delivered STL is watertight.
validation.direction: not applicable (inequality pins); the FEA underneath under-predicts deflection per the ace_fea pin.

caveats: Compliance-optimal is NOT strength-optimal: check as_built.max_von_mises_pa and re-run ace_fea on the STL for the load cases you actually have.
compliance_first is the UNIFORM-volfrac gray start, not the solid part — descent is measured against that start.
Thin members near the voxel size are resolution-limited (see ace_fea limits); the STL gate escalates mesh resolution until watertight or says why not.
The STL is a mesh only — no density-to-B-rep reconstruction exists; treat it as print/simulation geometry, not a parametric solid.

limits_of_validity.regime: linear-elastic stiffness design, single static load case, volfrac strictly inside (0,1)
limits_of_validity.slenderness: pinned at L/h = 5 cantilever; extreme aspect grids inherit the FEA's discretization limits
limits_of_validity.resolution: features below ~4 voxels across are unreliable; refine voxel_mm rather than trusting sub-voxel struts
